To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
hyperoxic environment induces morphological changes in Guinea pig kidneys and adrenal gland, which are correlated with the hyperoxia-induced oxidative stress.

the exposure of Guinea pigs to hyperbaric environment (1.5 ATA for 2 hours) induces morphological changes in kidney and adrenal gland, with direct implications upon their function, and that the changes are more pronounced in the suprarenal glands.

the morphometric and histological analysis of the kidney and adrenal gland of the Guinea pig exposed to the hyperbaric-hypoxic environment showed a significant decrease in the number of cells in the renal corpuscle, glomerular and cortical tubule, a reduction of the glomerular diameter, and a decrease of the diameter of the renal corpuscles, the glomerular and the cortical tubule.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the influence of the hyperoxic environment (with 100% oxygen) on the histological structure of the kidney and the adrenal gland, and on the morphometric study of the kidney and adrenal gland of the Guinea pig.
the study of the morphological changes of the kidney and adrenal gland in Guinea pig exposed to 3 ATA hyperbaric-hypoxic environment.
the study of the histological and morphometrical modifications in the kidney and adrenal gland of Guinea pig exposed to the hyperoxic environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the morphological changes of the kidney and adrenal gland are due to hyperoxia, which is the main factor of the hyperbaric-hypoxic environment.
hyperoxia induces oxidative stress in the kidneys and suprarenals of Guinea pig, which is reflected by the morphological changes of the two organs.

the exposure to a hyperbaric-hypoxic environment induces morphological changes in kidney and adrenal gland, which may be explained by the increased production of free oxygen species and by the vasoconstrictive effect of hyperoxia on renal afferent arteriolar vessels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

in hyperbarica-hyperoxic environment, the kidney and suprarenal gland undergo structural changes, with the most important ones being: glomerular atrophy, tubular dilatation, intertubular fibrosis and adrenal cortex hypertrophy.

the morphological changes in Guinea pig kidney and adrenal gland exposed to hyperoxic environment are the result of the increased free oxygen radicals production, with direct implications upon the cell metabolism.
the exposure to hyperbaric environment leads to a series of morphological changes in kidney and adrenal gland of Guinea pig, with direct implications in the cellular metabolism.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the morphological changes of the kidneys and adrenal gland in hyperbaric environment, as well as their correlation with the histological changes, could be a good indicator for the development of the disease and could be used as a prognostic factor.
the morphological changes are not specific, but they are the consequence of the hyperoxic environment, and not of the hyperbaric one.

hyperbaric hyperoxia can be considered as a risk factor for the kidney and suprareal glands, which is why it is important to monitor the evolution of these organs during the exposure of animals to hyperoxic environment.
